question: Mary Kom won her last international gold medal at which boxing competition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President’s Cup, Indonesia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mary Kom**, a legendary Indian boxer, won her last international gold medal at the **President’s Cup** held in **Indonesia in 2019**.
 
• The **President’s Cup** is an international boxing competition where top boxers from various countries participate. Mary Kom clinched the gold medal in the **51 kg category**.
 
• This victory demonstrated her remarkable skills, determination, and ability to perform at the highest level despite her age and years of competing in professional boxing.
 
• The competition was particularly significant for Mary Kom, as she was preparing for her participation in the **2020 Tokyo Olympics qualifiers**. Hence, this win boosted her confidence and underlined her dominance in the sport.
 
• Mary Kom is known for her exceptional career, including being a **six-time World Champion** and an Olympic medalist, and this gold medal added another feather to her illustrious cap.
 
• The other options listed, such as the **Asian Games, Hangzhou**, and **Commonwealth Games, Birmingham**, are prestigious events, but Mary Kom did not win her last gold medal at these events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Mary Kom:**

 
 
• **Full Name:** Chungneijang Mary Kom Hmangte.
 
• **Born:** November 24, 1982, in Manipur, India.
 
• Mary Kom is the only woman to become a **World Amateur Boxing Champion six times** and has won a medal in each of the first seven World Championships.
 
• She is also the first Indian woman boxer to win an **Olympic medal**, securing a bronze in the **2012 London Olympics**.
 
• In addition to her Olympic success, Mary Kom has won gold medals in the **Asian Games (2014)** and the **Commonwealth Games (2018)**.
 
 
 
• **President’s Cup, Indonesia:**
 
 
• The **President’s Cup** is an annual international boxing tournament held in Indonesia.
 
• It attracts top boxing talent from around the world and serves as an important platform for boxers to showcase their skills and prepare for major global competitions.
 
• In 2019, Mary Kom won the **gold medal** in the **51 kg category**, marking a significant achievement in her career.
 
 
 
• **Major Achievements of Mary Kom:**
 
 
• **Six-time World Champion:** Mary Kom has won the AIBA Women’s World Boxing Championship six times in various weight categories.
 
• **Olympic Medal:** She won a bronze medal in the **2012 London Olympics** in the flyweight (51 kg) category.
 
• **Asian Games Gold Medal:** Mary Kom won a gold medal in the **2014 Incheon Asian Games**.
 
• **Commonwealth Games Gold Medal:** She achieved this feat in the **2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games**.
 
• **Padma Awards:** She has been honored with the **Padma Shri (2006)**, **Padma Bhushan (2013)**, and **Padma Vibhushan (2020)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Preparation for Tokyo Olympics:** The **President’s Cup win** was a crucial part of Mary Kom’s preparation for the **2020 Tokyo Olympics qualifiers**. Although she couldn’t secure a medal in the Olympics, her performance in the qualifying stages was commendable.
 
• **Age and Legacy:** Despite being in her late 30s during her win at the President’s Cup, Mary Kom proved that age is not a barrier to achieving success in sports.
 
• **Inspiration:** Mary Kom’s achievements have inspired countless young athletes, especially women, to pursue careers in sports, breaking stereotypes and societal barriers.
